newsitem.title: UKRAINE: GM, DAEWOO to make cars jointly in Ukraine.
newsitem.headline: GM, DAEWOO to make cars jointly in Ukraine.

text.p: U.S. carmaker General Motors (GM) and South Korea's Daewoo Group will form a joint venture in Ukraine to produce cars at the AvtoZAZ car plant in the city of Zaporizhya, Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko said on Tuesday.
"There is the agreement, that Daewoo and General Motors will sign a deal and form a joint venture," Lazarenko told a news conference. "The plan is 220,000-255,000 cars annually in four years."

An investment tender to find a strategic investor for AvtoZAZ, Ukraine's only car plant, was officially announced earlier this year. Both Daewoo and GM had been considered the only serious contenders.
Lazarenko said that the official results of the tender would be announced by May 9.
He said GM would produce 35,000 Opels and 150,000 Daewoo cars in Zaporizhya, some 600 km (330 miles) south-east of Kiev.
Lazarenko added AvtoZAZ would produce its Tavria and Dana small city cars, but they would be modernised with the help of Daewoo and GM.
Sources close to the government said GM wanted to produce its Opel Vectra cars while Daewoo wanted to produce its Tico, Espero and Nexia models.
Senior Daewoo officials have said previously the Group was ready to invest up to $1 billion into AvtoZAZ.
